newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds continue reversal for now.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds continue reversal for now.

text.p: *Australian bond and bill futures ended after hours trading with minor falls as the market continued to wind back last week's strong rally, risking their recent rising channels.
*First of this week's two key events due with labour tribunal to hand down "living wage" claim verdict at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
Australian bond and bill futures ended after-hours trading with minor falls as the market continued to wind back last week's strong rally, risking their recent rising channels.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM at 92.110, only a shade below Monday's 92.115 pit close, but having dipped to 92.080 at one stage and the base line of this month's rising channel.
The contract now finds itself under some pressure after last week's 30 basis point rally stalled at 92.230, the top of a 92.210/92.230 congestion area.
The 92.230 level also represents a 50 percent retracement of the mid-February to early April sell-off from 92.760 to 91.700.

However, the fortunes of the market could quickly reverse on a fundamental basis with the first of this week's two key events due when the Australian Industrial Relations Commission hands down the "living wage" claim verdict at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

Economists expectations on the outcome centre on a A$12 per week safety net payment as a compromise to the government's A$8.0 per week proposal and the Australian Council of Trade Unions' A$20 per week safety net and 8.75 percent minimum rate adjustment claim.
An outcome of around A$12 per week is not seen giving the Reserve Bank undue concern over wage inflation as it would keep it within the Bank's 4.0-4.5 percent comfort zone.
The second crucial piece of information for the market which may give a clue to monetary policy will be Wednesday's release of the March quarter Consumer Price Index.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries finished lower as the market made ready for Tuesday's auction of US$17.0 billion of two-year notes and Wednesday's sale of US$12.5 billion of five-year notes.
